subject: Pre-QBR metric alignment: ownership, risk signals, and action items
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: alice.monroe@acme.com, ops-support@acme.com
Date: Sat, 02 Sep 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pre-QBR metric alignment: ownership, risk signals, and action items

Team — attaching the August KPI pack ahead of the QBR next week. High level asks below; please confirm owners and ETA for the action items by EOD Monday. I copied Acme's ops leads to surface their production concerns.

Attachments: QBR_KPI_Dashboard_2028-08.pdf, kpi-drilldowns-2028-08.xlsx

Top-level signals (high-priority):
- Latency: median is steady at 42ms but P95 rose from 210ms -> 375ms for long contexts (>1024). Suspect batching skew and a few kernel regressions on warm-starts. (owner: jonas_weber)
- Cost: cost-per-1M tokens normalized increased 14% month-over-month driven by higher retry rates on a small set of heavy customers; caching hit-rate dropped from 61% -> 48%. (owner: jasmine_liu)
- Uptime: platform availability 99.96% for Aug; two brief infra incidents (total 28m) mostly in eu-west. Need RCA for one incident and remediation plan. (owner: marissa_cole)
- Usage: active seats up 18% with a 12% increase in long-sequence requests; ephemeral KV pressure noted in Dedicated pools.

Concrete asks (please reply inline with owner + ETA):
1) Jonas: initial mitigation for P95 spike (can we roll temporary kernel fallback to previous release for long contexts?) — ETA?
2) Jasmine: quick triage on caching regression and risky query patterns by Tuesday; list top 10 customers contributing to retry delta. Also propose short-term config to raise prefix cache TTL.
3) Marissa: one-pager RCA for the Aug 12 outage and proposed SLA guardrails (due Wednesday).
4) Me (Kimberly): will draft the leadership one-page highlighting risks and what we will commit to in the QBR. Please send any slides/notes by Tuesday noon.

Customer note (Acme): Alice, thanks for flagging latency degradation in your Prod region — we prioritized this in the pack and will surface owner-level contact. Expect a follow-up from Jonas with immediate mitigation steps.

Thanks — Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Head of Platform Ops
Redwood Inference

--
[attachment: QBR_KPI_Dashboard_2028-08.pdf] [attachment: kpi-drilldowns-2028-08.xlsx]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>

Cc: alice.monroe@acme.com
Date: Sat, 02 Sep 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pre-QBR metric alignment: ownership, risk signals, and action items

Kimberly — thanks for the clear summary. Quick notes / commitments:

- P95 spike: I can push a targeted kernel rollback for long-context requests to the eu/us Dedicated pools as a temporary mitigation. It avoids a full rollback and should shave ~120–160ms off P95 based on canary runs. ETA to schedule: Monday 04:00 UTC (will be after a brief smoke test). If we see adverse side effects, we'll rollback the change and revert to plan B (workload-specific batching cap).

- I'll open a short-lived diag runbook and share logs for the 10 heaviest long-context traces by EOD Monday.

Notes for Acme: Alice — we'll prioritize your region; expect a direct note with the mitigation window and contact details.

Jonas
Senior SRE — Serving Runtime

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 02 Sep 2028 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pre-QBR metric alignment: ownership, risk signals, and action items

Kim / team — I pulled the cache and retry slices; quick summary:

- Root cause signal: a config change on Aug 3 increased conservative cache invalidation for objects with low TTLs; combined with a spike in long prompts from two customers (Acme + BetaLabs) the effective cache hit dropped.
- Top contributors to retry delta: acme.com (23%), betalabs.ai (11%), internal integration tests (7%). Full top-10 attached in the spreadsheet.

Short-term mitigations (I can action Monday before Jonas' rollback):
1) Bump prefix cache TTL for long-context descriptors from 30s -> 180s (safe for most customers) — low risk, rolled config by 14:00 PDT Monday if no objections.
2) Add a lightweight retry budget for very long requests to avoid cost cascades (proposal in spreadsheet).

I'll own the config roll and produce a before/after telemetry snapshot for the QBR. ETA: changes applied and snapshot by Mon 22:00 UTC.

Jasmine
Sr. Product Ops Engineer

Subject: Re: Pre-QBR metric alignment: ownership, risk signals, and action items

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for looping us in. A couple of clarifications from our side:

- The latency impact for us is most pronounced on batched inference for our summarization pipeline; P95 regressions correlate with certain prompt shapes that include long context anchors. Happy to share examples — I put three trace IDs in the ops-support mailbox.
- The uptime blips on Aug 12 overlapped with our nightly heavy-sync job; if there's any plan to increase staged retries please flag us so we can stagger our sync.

Appreciate the ownership. We look forward to Jonas' mitigation window and Jasmine's cache TTL change.

Alice Monroe
Head of Platform Engineering
Acme Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 03 Sep 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pre-QBR metric alignment: ownership, risk signals, and action items

Quick status update:

- RCA for Aug 12 incident: working draft completed. Initial finding points to a transient routing flapping in the eu-west networking layer triggered by a noisy health-check loop from a partner agent. Draft RCA and remediation plan attached to Drive link (see related_links). Final one-pager to Kimberly by Wed EOD.
- SLA guardrails: proposing a per-region rolling deploy window + mandatory canary for kernel changes that impact long-context paths — draft policy in the drive doc, send comments by Tuesday.

I'll sync with ops-support (Acme) to confirm whether their sync coincided with the event; that will help shape recommended guardrails.

Marissa
Director, Reliability Engineering
